meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about his zero from his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. That's procedure 4.2, and I'm writing down that you admit it. Now, on what basis is there a zero at all?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
A wrong quotation is a citation error, Hale, and seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare every week. Show me the page it's on in Owen's essay. And what else do you have, because that isn't a zero.
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.

You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence, Hale. Claire won her appeal, and you just told me this "seems to run in the family", which I'm writing down word for word. When we're done here, I'm going to the principal's office with it.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn, an apology, and a written assurance that nothing goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: back at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and nothing on Owen's record, with a visit to the principal planned.
What moved her: "I should have called you before entering the zero", because owning the process in one sentence earned a flat okay and a real question about the basis.
What cost ground: "It seems to run in the family", because bringing up Claire attacked her family and sent her straight back to the principal.
Try next time: after naming the line that "isn't anywhere in Hamlet", put the page of Owen's essay in front of her with its date instead of mentioning Claire.
